text.p: French Prime Minister Alain Juppe, presenting the centre-right coalition's parliamentary election platform, said on Tuesday that creating jobs would remain "our obsession".

"Employment has been and will remain our obsession," he said in a speech to members of the coalition at a convention hall. "But the answer to unemployment will not come from the old 1980s formulas -- cutting the work week, multiplying the number of public sector jobs. That's a recipe for certain failure."

"The real answer can only come from business and from individual initiatives. To create more jobs, we need to create and develop more businesses. All the current examples, all the the past examples show it."

Juppe said the government had taken steps over the past four years to ease unemployment, now at a record 12.8 percent, by lowering social security contribution charges, making working hours more flexible and encouraging small and medium sized companies.
But he said these measures had been insufficient to meet the increase in the active working population.
